newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Union banka lists shares on Belgrade bourse.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Union banka lists shares on Belgrade bourse.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Union banka has joined a group of three other banks on the Belgrade Stock Exchange by listing its shares on the BSE late in February, the bourse said on Tuesday.
"Union banka listed one million dinars ($177,314) in preference shares on February 26," BSE General Manager Pava Zecevic told reporters.
Each share has a 500 dinar face value.
"Union banka is a medium-sized, strong, joint stock bank, without an old hard currency savings burden and active in financing exports," BSE spokesman Milko Stimac told Reuters.
But despite listing its shares on February 26, the bank has not found buyers for its stock yet.

Kulska banka, AIK banka and Panonska banka listed a total of 29.5 million dinars in ordinary shares early in February, putting an end to an almost year long period without any share trading on the BSE.
Analysts said share trading resembled more a private placing with issuers mostly completing pre-arranged deals on the bourse.
Commercial banks and companies are obliged to sell part of their issued stock on the bourse to meet new rules set by the Yugoslav Securities Commission (YSC) last November.
In an attempt to speed up development of the local financial market, YSC said it would qualify a share issue as successful only if part of the issue is listed and sold on the bourse.

Apart from shares, which boosted the February turnover on the Belgrade bourse and accounted for 22 percent of the 134.307 million dinars total monthly turnover, the BSE also trades in commodities and financial instruments. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
